24-HOUR LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST Issued at:      4:00 PM October 09, 2026  Valid Until:    4:00 PM Tomorrow SYNOPSIS:  At 3:00 PM today, a Low Pressure Area (LPA) was estimated based on all avilable data at 520 km East of Catarman, Northern Samar (12.6°N 129.4°E). It is embedded along the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) affecting Visayas,  Palawan, DAVAO REGION and the rest of Mindanao. Northeasterly Windflow affecting the eastern sections of Northern and Central Luzon. FORECAST: DAVAO REGION will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to ITCZ. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains.  Light to Moderate winds coming from the Northwest to Southwest will prevail and the coastal water  will be Slight to Moderate (0.6 to 1.8 meters wave height). KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN: Ang Dakbayan sa Davao ug ubang dapit sa DAVAO REGION makasinati ug mapanganuron nga kalangitan nga adunay mga pagdag-um inubanan sa katag-katag nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa ITCZ. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa  kusog nga pagbundak sa ulan. Hinay ngadto sa Kasarangan nga huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa Amihanang-Kasadpan ngadto sa Habagatang-Kasadpan nga direksyon ang mopasulabi ug ang kadagatan mahimong Hapsay ngadto sa Kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.8 meters wave height). Human sa nahitabo nga kaylap nga pagbaha sa dakong bahin sa Luzon niining bag-ohay nga mga adlaw, gimando ni Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. ang hugot nga pagpatuman sa mga balaod nga may kalabotan sa urban planning, ilabi na sa mga kritikal nga lugar sa tibuok nasod nga kanunay gibahaan. Sa gipahigayon nga media conference niining Martes, Septyembre 1, miingon si Palace Press Officer Atty. Claire Castro nga kini nga paghugot sa pagpatuman sa balaod sa urban planning gihisgutan sa miting ni PBBM uban sa nagkalain-laing ahensya sa gobyerno nga nangita og solusyon sa dakong problema sa pagbaha sa Metro Manila ug ubang mga lugar. “Kung nasunod lamang daw ang mga ito ay maaaring ang mga lugar na dapat tayuan ng mga imprastraktura at mga lugar na bahain ang dapat manatiling libre at walang imprastrakctura para siya ang tumanggap ng tubig-ulan,” giit ni Castro. Matud niya, adunay mga master plan na sa urban development nga nahimo alang sa Metro Manila sukad pa niadtong 1941 ug 1956 alang sa Cebu apan wala kini mapatuman, hinungdan nga nakatukod og mga imprastraktura ug mga puy-anan sa mga lugar nga nakasamok sa hapsay nga pag-agos sa tubig gikan sa mga suba ug estero. “Huwag nang mamulitika. Ipatupad na ang batas. At dapat ipaliwanag sa lahat na maging istrikto sap ag-implementa ng batas para sa ating kaligtasan,” dugang niya. ============= Matapos naganap ang malawakang pagbaha sa malaking bahagi ng Luzon nitong mga nakaraang araw, ipinag-utos na Pangulong Ferdinand R. METRO MANILA FACES SEVERE INUNDATION DESPITE PREVIOUS DISASTER FOCUS ON MINDANAO Netizens Contrast NCR Flood Crisis with Normal Daily Life in Davao City Following Palace Statements MANILA, Philippines — Heavy downpours have left vast portions of Metro Manila submerged, sparking renewed public discussion over recent statements by Presidential Communications Office Undersecretary Castro regarding regional flood vulnerabilities. Earlier comments from Usec. Castro highlighted Davao as a primary center for flooding concerns in the country. However, current conditions show the National Capital Region bearing the brunt of severe waterlogging, causing major traffic disruptions and stranded commuters across key thoroughfares. Meanwhile, viral footage and social media posts show residents in Davao City enjoying routine outdoor activities, including community basketball games, under manageable weather conditions. Local authorities in Metro Manila are currently deploying emergency teams and pumps to clear inundated avenues, while disaster management officials reiterate that flood monitoring remains active nationwide regardless of shifting weather patterns. LOOK:|BEHIND EVERY NUMBER: THE HUMAN HEARTBREAK OF NEPAL’S FLASH FLOOD. August 29, 2026 — One can scarcely imagine the terror: standing inside your own home, hearing the roar of water, mud, and rocks approaching — and having only seconds to wonder if your family will survive. That was the reality for communities along the Nepal–Tibet border on August 26, 2026, when a massive glacier and rock collapse triggered a catastrophic flash flood along the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi rivers. Homes, roads, bridges, power plants, and entire settlements were swept away — often with little or no warning.  IN THOSE FINAL MOMENTS Residents were forced to scramble to rooftops, balconies, or any higher ground available — clinging to hope as waters rose nearly 30 feet in half an hour. We may never fully know what went through their minds: Were they crying? Calling loved ones? Praying? Holding each other? What we do know is that behind every statistic is a human life, a family, and a story of heartbreak.  THE SCALE OF LOSS - 469 confirmed dead — and still rising - Hundreds more remain missing, including tourists and pilgrims from several nations - Entire communities buried under mud and debris - Rescue teams continue to reach isolated areas "Behind every number is a family waiting. Behind every missing person is someone desperately hoping. And behind every survivor is a story of courage."  May rescuers reach those still waiting. May the missing be found. And may every grieving family find strength in this time of unimaginable loss.  ,///Charlie. #PrayForNepal #NepalFlood #HimalayanDisaster #FlashFlood #DisasterAwareness #HopeAndPrayer #BosesNgPilipinas See less LOOK:|BEHIND EVERY NUMBER: THE HUMAN HEARTBREAK OF NEPAL’S FLASH FLOOD.

DAVAO: THE “FLOOD CAPITAL” — BUT PERHAPS NOT FOR THE REASON YOU THINK They say Davao is the “Flood Capital of the Philippines.” Well, if someone insists on giving us that crown, perhaps we should wear it proudly—but let’s first ask a simple question: What exactly is overflowing?  Yes, Davao experiences floods. We have rivers that swell after relentless rain, low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature, sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment, and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools. That is a real problem. It deserves real solutions—not political theater. But if we are going to compare cities, perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan. During the severe southwest monsoon flooding in July 2025, for example, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across Metro Manila within a single day. So before anyone points a finger at Davao, perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city. Water does not check political affiliations before it rises. Rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours. And rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches.  But here's where I see Davao differently. Because there is another kind of flooding happening here—one that doesn't destroy homes, close roads, or leave mud behind. Davao floods with culture. Walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of Mindanao: Indigenous traditions, migrant communities, different languages, cuisines, beliefs, stories, and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry. Ask someone where they came from, and you may discover an entire story behind the answer. Then, inevitably, there's food. Because in Davao, you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian.  “This variety is sweeter.” “No, that one has better texture.” “You haven't tried the best one yet.” Suddenly, what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian. No registration fee required.  But perhaps Davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture. It is warmth. There is a quiet generosity in the character of many Dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure. You can arrive as a stranger and, before long, someone may already be telling you where to eat, what places to visit, which shortcut to take—and, most importantly, which road to avoid when traffic is terrible. That's not just hospitality. That's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory.  And then there is Davao's natural beauty. The sea. Samal. Mount Apo. The forests. The farms. The rivers. The mountains. The wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies. Davao is also changing. Businesses are arriving. Buildings are rising. Infrastructure is expanding. Communities are growing. People continue to come—not only because they are looking for jobs, but because they are looking for possibilities. Some arrive carrying résumés. Others arrive carrying business plans. Some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream. And somewhere along the way, many discover something unexpected: They don't merely live in Davao. They become part of it. That, perhaps, is the real story. A city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it. It should also be judged by what its people continue to build despite those problems. Davao is not perfect. We have traffic. We have growing pains. We have environmental concerns. We have infrastructure challenges. We have political disagreements. And, of course, we have social-media experts who can apparently repair the entire country using nothing but a smartphone and a Facebook account.  But beneath all the noise is something far more difficult to construct: Character. You can build a highway. You can build skyscrapers. You can build malls, bridges, offices, and massive developments. You can even build a spectacular roundabout that everyone will complain about for months.  But you cannot manufacture belonging. You cannot pour it into concrete. You cannot buy it from a catalog. It has to grow. And Davao has grown through people. People from different places came here. They planted roots. They built families. They opened businesses. They raised children. They created communities. And little by little, their individual stories became part of the larger story of the city. For the past 15 years, I have had the privilege of traveling around Davao for team-building activities, retreats, seminars, workshops, and speaking engagements. And in those years, I have seen something that no flood statistics can capture. I have seen people flood others with smiles, generosity, and warmth. So if someone wants to call Davao the “Flood Capital of the Philippines,” perhaps we shouldn't be offended. Maybe we should simply redefine the flood. text: 10/9 7AM Update: Hurricane Isaias has strengthened into a major Category 3 hurricane with max sustained winds of 120 mph. The storm will begin weakening prior to landfall along our coast this evening, but it will still be a SIGNIFICANT hurricane upon impact.  All last minute preparations should be rushed to completion this morning. Residents and tourists should follow the advice given by local officials and evacuate immediately if told to do so.  Here are the latest details:  Timing & Track: Deteriorating conditions through the day today with rain spreading north and tropical storm force winds starting as early as noon. The worst conditions are expected from late afternoon through late evening as the center makes landfall, likely between Mobile Bay and Choctawhatchee Bay.  Storm Surge: Potential for 6-9 feet for the western Florida Panhandle, 4-6 ft for the Alabama coastline, and 3-5 ft for Mobile Bay. Surge will be highest near and east of the track, while areas west of the track may experience low water levels around landfall.  Winds: Upon approach, widespread tropical storm force winds and wind damage will occur well away from the center, with damaging hurricane-force winds near the center close to the coast. Expect winds to cause structural damage and knock down trees/powerlines, leading numerous power outages.  Flooding: Heavy rain near the core of the storm and in bands well east of the center could cause significant flash flooding, especially on saturated ground and in urban areas. Storm total rainfall amounts, generally around 4-8 inches for areas east of the Alabama River; highest by the coast. Localized totals up to 12 inches are possible, particularly near/just west of the track.  Tornadoes: An increased threat of several tornadoes exists late afternoon into tonight for areas east of I-65 within the outer bands.   Beach Hazards: HIGH risk of strong life-threatening rip currents through the weekend with dangerous surf (20+ ft breakers east of the center) expected through Saturday. Major to extreme beach erosion is expected. *Be Prepared, Not Scared.*  Refer to our tropical webpage for the latest information on local impacts: https://www.weather.gov/srh/tropical?office=mob#hti  See our latest briefing slides: https://www.weather.gov/mob/dsspacket See less 10/9 7AM Update: Hurricane Isaias has strengthened into a major Category 3 hurricane with max sustained winds of 120 mph. DAVAO FLOODING IS NOT A CORRUPTION ISSUE 1. IT IS a calamity issue - Singapore, the US, Dubai, and other cities also had their fair share of flooding - For Davao, it rained heavily for at least 5 nights, thunderstorms, almost all night. But flooding did not happen until the 4th or 5th night.  This means, of course, the ground is loose, basins are filled, and calamities can occur. - Flooding happened in areas close to the river and low-lying areas, which is a small portion of the whole city. Only 358 families were reported to be affected.  - But for Davao, we had minimal effects. If this had happened elsewhere, it could have been worse. Our LGU learned from the 2011 incident. Our 51-B flood control project protected MILLIONS of us.  2. IT IS NOT a Preparedness-Issue - Unlike other cities, our LGU has a world-class disaster and risk management plan.  - Our 911 is world-class. - Our disaster and rescue facilities and equipment are world-class - Talk about our taxes-well spent - Talk about the years of good governance of the  City Government of Davao - Living in Davao, we feel safe even in calamities, knowing that our LGU will have early warning protocols, search and rescue operations directives, and the PEOPLE OF DAVAO who are there to help each other. - Yes, even if our LGU is there, Davaoeños are also there for the government and for each other. This is why Davao has eagle-like resilience. 3. IT IS NOT a Governance-Issue -  Davao has a working City Social Services and Development Office (CCSDO). It is an exclusive arm of the city to take care of us in case of any fire, flood, or other calamities. - They are seen and felt. They are usually first on the ground to give warm food, clothing, mental health assistance, etc., during disasters. - Baranggay and city officials are mostly on the ground before, during, and after a calamity to facilitate and assist their residents in getting back to its feet. One family at a time, one day at a time. - Suppliers like water,  power, (internet - not so sure), will do their best to restore services asap. OUR CITY OFFICIALS, the Dutertes, are not corrupt and poor in their governance.  This city can withstand trials because we were built to withstand any, YESTERDAY, not when disasters strike. Will calamities hit the city? Big YES! Will we be affected by it?  Also YES! Is our LGU perfect? NO. Is our LGU dependable in times of crisis? Big YES! The effect is not as bad. Because of the last few decades of being raised by the Dutertes, this city is positioned to be forward-thinking. We were able to build this city surge into any economic and natural disaster challenges. So stop bashing the city with its small hit as if it has fallen big time, because even if we were hit, good governance has protected many. This is not like your city, and our experience is not like yours, which shaped your current judgment. And NO, this is not a "zombie-type" and blind following a persona, a name, or a party. Davaoeños are better than that. We will hold our leaders accountable if they mess up.  So stop using a calamity-based hit to shape a political narrative that doesn't exist just to forward an evil notion to destroy credibility and positioning. That's not gonna withstand, because OUR TRUTH is what we experience here daily, backed by YEARS OF GENERALLY A BETTER QUALITY OF LIFE. #davaocity  #raisedbyaduterte   SunStar Davao ,  Davao Today , Ry Llanes,  MindaNews , Kgwd Raymund Carin Gumanid,  GMA Regional TV News Personal Note: Davao is not "better" than other places. PUMP BOY NAKURYENTEHAN, NALUMOS SA BAHA SA BUHANGIN  A 21-year-old pump boy was found lifeless after reportedly being electrocuted and drowning in floodwaters in New San Isidro, Barangay Buhangin, Davao City at around 2:35 AM on May 19, 2026. The victim, a single man from Manay, Davao Oriental, was reportedly renting a place in the area when the incident occurred. Police from Station 5 – Buhangin, together with barangay responders and Central 911 rescue teams, were conducting flood monitoring and rescue operations when they discovered the victim floating in front of his boarding house around 2:00 AM. He was immediately brought to the Southern Philippines Medical Center (SPMC), but was later declared dead by attending physicians. His cause of death was listed as cardiopulmonary arrest secondary to fatal cardiac dysrhythmia due to electrocution, with acute respiratory failure secondary to drowning. "OO, RESIDENTE AKO NG DAVAO CITY"  Kinuwestiyon ni dating Philippine National Police (PNP) Chief Nicolas Torre III ang patuloy na pagbaha sa Davao City matapos muling bahain ang kanyang bahay sa NHA Bangkal, Barangay Talomo kasunod ng malakas na ulan noong Hulyo 24. Sa kanyang social media post, sinabi ni Torre na nakapangalan sa kanya at sa kanyang asawa ang naturang bahay at bilang residente ng Davao City ay may karapatan siyang magtanong kung bakit paulit-ulit pa ring nangyayari ang pagbaha. Ayon kay Torre, matagal nang alam na ang mga sanhi ng pagbaha tulad ng mountain runoff at malalakas na pag-ulan, kaya dapat aniya ay may epektibong solusyon na, lalo na't bilyon-bilyong piso na ang nagastos para sa mga flood control projects. Binigyang-diin niya na ang tunay na sukatan ng flood control ay hindi ang dami ng proyektong naipatupad kundi ang dami ng pamilyang hindi na naaabot ng baha. "Naghahanap ako ng resulta, hindi ng palusot," saad ni Torre. #LNB See less "OO, RESIDENTE AKO NG DAVAO CITY"

Claire Castro na hindi magdadalawang isip si Pangulong Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. na tulungan ang Davao City na maresolba ang umano'y malubhang pagbaha sa nasabing siyudad. Sa isang press briefing nitong Agosto 27, 2026, sinabi ni Castro na inatasan ng Pangulo si Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon na tignan kung ano ang maaring gawing aksyon sa Davao City. "So, lahat naman po ng lugar sa Pilipinas na binabaha ay tinutugunan ng ating pamahalaan at iyan po ang utos ng Pangulong Marcos Jr. Kaya nga po noong sumobra ang baha sa Davao City, hindi naman po nagpatumpik-tumpik ang Pangulo at si Secretary Vince Dizon, na tulungan na ang Davao City dahil malubha na rin po ang pagbaha sa Davao," ani Castro. Maliban dito ay sinabi rin ni Castro ang kahalagahan ng mga dokumento upang malaman kung ano ba talaga ang naging progreso ng mga flood control project sa Davao City.
